clinicalPearls: Consists of cholesterol crystals that form within a liquefied (synchytic) vitreous, characteristically in an eye already damaged by previous trauma, chronic vitreous haemorrhage or long-standing severe intraocular disease
Crystals are flat, angular and golden-brown or multicoloured with a highly refractile glitter, in contrast to the round white spheres of asteroid hyalosis
Because the vitreous is liquefied the crystals move freely and settle inferiorly under gravity when the eye is still, then swirl through the cavity on movement like a snow-globe
Often unilateral when secondary to prior injury or haemorrhage in one eye, but may be bilateral where systemic or metabolic factors contribute
Typically arises in an eye with vision already reduced by the underlying disease; the crystals themselves seldom cause additional visual loss
Cholesterol crystals may also accumulate in the anterior chamber (cholesterolosis) in a blind or severely damaged eye
Diagnosis is essentially clinical, and management is directed at the underlying condition rather than at the inert crystals themselves
reference.pathophysiology: Synchysis scintillans, or cholesterolosis bulbi, develops when cholesterol released from the breakdown of blood or degenerating tissue after haemorrhage, trauma or chronic intraocular disease crystallises within a vitreous that has already undergone liquefaction. Loss of the normal gel structure allows the dense crystals to move freely and to sediment inferiorly under gravity between eye movements. It therefore signifies a previously diseased eye, distinguishing it from asteroid hyalosis, in which calcium-phospholipid bodies remain suspended in a still-formed gel and do not settle.
additionalDifferentials: Asteroid hyalosis (calcium soaps suspended in a formed gel that do not sediment)
Retained intraocular foreign body or changes of long-standing retinal detachment
additionalInvestigations: Slit-lamp and dilated fundus examination noting settling of crystals inferiorly at rest
B-scan ultrasonography demonstrating mobile echoes that settle with gravity, particularly where the fundus view is poor
Detailed history and examination for previous trauma, haemorrhage or chronic intraocular disease
Examination of the fellow eye to assess laterality and any systemic pattern
Investigation of the underlying cause of recurrent or chronic vitreous haemorrhage where relevant
Fundus imaging where the media are clear enough to document the crystals and underlying retina
redFlags: Recurrent or new vitreous haemorrhage indicating active underlying disease such as proliferative retinopathy or a retinal tear
Signs of a retained intraocular foreign body or occult penetrating trauma
A painful blind eye raising concern about other end-stage complications
New visual symptoms in the fellow eye
reference.prognosis: The cholesterol crystals themselves are inert and generally do not threaten vision; the visual outcome is determined almost entirely by the underlying ocular disease that gave rise to them. Many affected eyes already have poor vision from the causative pathology.
pitfalls: Confusing it with asteroid hyalosis and missing the clue that a liquefied vitreous with sedimenting crystals signifies a previously diseased eye
Overlooking a treatable underlying cause of recurrent vitreous haemorrhage
Attempting to treat the crystals rather than the primary pathology
Failing to examine the fellow eye and assess for systemic contributors
references: Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach
management: No treatment is directed at the inert cholesterol crystals themselves, and asymptomatic eyes are simply observed
Direct management at the underlying ocular disease, treating the cause of recurrent or chronic vitreous haemorrhage and the sequelae of prior trauma
Reserve pars plana vitrectomy for cases where crystals or media opacity obscure the view or where vitreoretinal pathology needs surgical treatment
Investigate the cause of recurrent vitreous haemorrhage where relevant
Monitor the affected eye and examine the fellow eye to assess laterality and any systemic contribution
Set realistic expectations, as visual prognosis is determined by the underlying disease rather than the crystals
